version.note: The catalogue describes mixed voices with orchestra, but no performing edition, arranger or individual instruments are established. No specific orchestral substitution or match to Handel’s original scoring is inferred from that generic credit.

performers.note: Densmore’s catalogue transcription describes Edison 80292-R as ‘Mixed voices with orchestra — Oratorio Chorus’. The orchestra’s identity, conductor and individual players are not credited; Edison is the record company, not a performer.

date.note: May 1916 is the release month, not an established session month. The year-level museum session date is retained.

place.note: No session venue is stated in the consulted museum or archive record.

label.note: The current museum catalogue identifies a disc; an early Commons upload comment calling it a cylinder is not followed.

matrixTakeSides.note: Museum transcription retained without silently interpreting every suffix as a take number.

credits.value: National Park Service source; Ogg conversion credited to Commons user Pmx
credits.note: The NPS is identified as the source, not a named transfer engineer. Commons explicitly credits Pmx for Ogg conversion only.

date.note: No transfer date is established; upload dates are not used as transfer dates.

processing.value: The upstream file is a 96 kbps MP3; Commons supplies an Ogg conversion and an MP3 access derivative.
processing.note: No de-clicking, equalisation or speed correction is documented. Successive lossy formats limit timbral comparison.

digital.format: Wikimedia Commons MP3 derivative of an Ogg conversion of the archive MP3

composition.value: Handel’s eighteenth-century underlying composition is out of copyright under the ordinary life-plus-70 term.
composition.note: The programme note identifies Handel as 1685–1759; this does not clear a later arrangement.

recording.value: United States public domain: Edison 80292-R was first released in May 1916.
recording.note: Programme rule 2; the museum establishes record and issue month. The upstream archive also carries the historic Creative Commons public-domain dedication URL, not a non-commercial licence. The generic Commons PD-US notice is not used to apply a printed-work cutoff to a sound recording.
